target: Akita AI data center (developer: BitGrid / S2)
description: Planned ~500MW AI data centre in Akita, northern Japan, that would be the country's largest. Developed by US startup BitGrid and Akita-based IT firm S2. Mubadala (via its MGX platform) is in talks to invest up to ~$6.3B of a reported ~$12.6B total project cost. Not finalized; Mubadala has declined to comment.

Global data-center operator with ~4GW live/under development and 6GW planned, formed in 2019 from Infomart and T5 assets by IPI Partners; IPI was acquired by Blue Owl Capital in 2024. Pursuing multibillion-dollar debt deals (Australia, Melbourne) to fund AI-driven buildout; sold its European colocation business to Apollo-managed funds in 2025.

Data-center buildout by HUMAIN, the Saudi PIF-owned AI company (launched May 2025, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman) building the full AI stack. Unconfirmed sources report a ~$5.3B Goldman Sachs-arranged financing to fund ~2GW of Riyadh-area data centers and GPUs, part of a 2034 capacity target; HUMAIN and Goldman have not confirmed terms.

target: NextEra Energy (Duane Arnold Energy Center restart)
description: NextEra Energy's 615MW Iowa nuclear plant, shut since 2020, is set for restart by Q1 2029 pending NRC licensing. The US DOE closed an up-to-$1.9B loan (announced Sept 8, 2026) to fund the restart; Google separately signed a 25-year agreement to buy the plant's power.

target: U.S. scientific research institutions / DOE Genesis Mission
description: DOE's Genesis Mission (created by executive order, directed by Under Secretary for Science Darío Gil) links national labs, universities and industry on AI-for-science; 278 projects were selected in July 2026. NVIDIA pledged $1B over five years (Oct 8, 2026) toward university research, US quantum computing, and government-research cloud providers under the mission, with no public breakdown by institution.

target: Grand Ming Group Holdings (iTech Tower 3.1 & 3.2, Fanling, Hong Kong -- via subsidiaries Regal Development Ltd & Golden Ford Ltd)
description: Hong Kong-listed (HKEX:1271) construction/property group. Its subsidiaries Regal Development and Golden Ford agreed to sell the iTech Tower 3.1 & 3.2 data-center project in Fanling (~185,000 sq ft, ~1,000 racks) to Amazon Data Services Hong Kong for a minimum HK$2.18B (~$277.9M, up to ~$311.7M), after earlier talks with Bain Capital and Actis lapsed.

target: UK AI safety research (BOLD at Oxford; SOFAIR at UCL; Imperial College London)
description: NVIDIA's five-year, $250M compute-access commitment (announced Oct 14, 2026, delivered via UK-based NVIDIA Cloud Partners) to UK AI safety and security research. Supports Oxford-led BOLD (human-AI collaboration), UCL's SOFAIR (with Cambridge, Oxford and Edinburgh), and Imperial College's safety-engineering/robotics work. This is a compute donation, not cash; specific allocations are still to be announced.

Advanced-nuclear developers named as partners in Project Prometheus, a DOE Genesis Mission initiative led by Idaho National Laboratory to apply AI to reactor design, licensing and operations. X-Energy is a Tier 1 partner contributing $10M in private capital and its Xe-100 small modular reactor design; the project's federal Phase II award is $60M, with ~$200M in industry cost-share cited by INL.

Nasdaq-listed (DGXX) AI data-center and crypto-mining company building a 40MW AI data center in Columbiana, Alabama, fully contracted to Cerebras. Received a $200M debt-financing commitment letter (Oct 13, 2026; Goldman Sachs syndicating) to complete the project — a project-SPV loan still subject to lender diligence and definitive documentation, not yet closed.

target: Idaho National Laboratory -- Project Prometheus (partners: NVIDIA, AWS, X-Energy)
description: DOE national lab leading Project Prometheus, the largest Phase II award ($60M over three years) under the Genesis Mission, aligning 32 labs, universities and companies — including NVIDIA, AWS, X-Energy, Oklo and other SMR developers — to apply AI to nuclear reactor design, licensing, manufacturing and semi-autonomous operation.

doxx.net, a privacy-focused networking startup founded by Barrett Lyon (previously Prolexic, BitGravity, Defense.net), raised a Series A — reported as $38M by most outlets, $24.6M per one source — led by a16z (Oct 2026), to launch its Agentic Defined Networking platform for private, policy-controlled connectivity for people and AI agents.

Melbourne data-center campus (reported ~252MW, MEL02) operated by Blue Owl-owned Stack Infrastructure. Stack mandated banks (Oct 15, 2026) for a five-year A$8.6B (~$6B) syndicated loan, one of the largest reported AI data-center debt deals; sources disagree on whether proceeds target MEL02 or MEL01, and the financing is not yet closed.

San Francisco AI-research startup (roughly 14-17 people) building reinforcement-learning environments resistant to reward hacking, including an open-source framework called Karotte, for frontier AI labs. Emerged from stealth Oct 7, 2026 with a $16M seed round led by a16z; co-investor lists vary by source (SignalFire, South Park Commons, Scale Angels, or Manifund, MoE Capital), plus angels including Fei-Fei Li.

Alphabet-spun-out AI drug-discovery company developing the IsoDDE drug design engine, targeting first clinical trials by end of 2026. Closed a $2.1B Series B (May 12, 2026) led by Thrive Capital, with Alphabet, GV, MGX, Temasek, CapitalG and the UK Sovereign AI Fund participating; previously raised $600M in its first round, also led by Thrive.

Cambridge, MA robotics startup co-founded by MIT's Pulkit Agrawal and Tuomas Haarnoja, building a 'Vision-Force-Action' model for dexterous manipulation, claiming superhuman pick rates on lab tasks. Raised a $150M Series A at a $1.45B valuation (Oct 20, 2026), led by a16z and F-Prime (one source names Fine Structure Ventures instead), with Samsung Next, Bison Ventures and others participating.

Asia-Pacific data-center operator spun out of GDS Holdings (independent since Jan 2025; GDS retains ~35.6%), with ~480MW live/building and ~590MW planned across Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Japan. Abu Dhabi's MGX explored a multibillion-dollar acquisition (reported June 2026), but DayOne is also pursuing a US IPO targeting a ~$20B valuation; no deal confirmed.

AI startup founded by Thiel Fellow Sigil Wen, maker of Underdog, an on-device personal-AI assistant (Mac/Windows invite-only beta) designed to keep user data off third-party AI clouds. a16z led its first funding round (Oct 2, 2026, undisclosed size), with Khosla Ventures, Hummingbird and the Anthropic/Menlo Anthology Fund also participating.

AI-driven autonomous red-team/offensive-security startup founded Sept 2025 by Mandiant founder Kevin Mandia. Raised a $255.5M Series B (Oct 1, 2026) co-led by a16z and Accel at a valuation above $2.5B, following ~$190M in earlier seed/Series A funding (also led by Accel); total funding is roughly $445M. Serves enterprise and government customers.
